title: Importing a graph from gml format does not set edge labels
description:
GML format files may have labels for edges, e.g.,

```
edge [
  source 1
  target 2
  label "e"
  value e
]
```

In function `import_graph` for GML files, the label attribute for edges appears not to be applied to the graph. In the source code for this function, lines 308-317 appear to extract the label string from each edge into vector `edge_label`. But in lines 340-348 where edge objects are created, there are no lines that set the `label` attribute of edges with this vector.

In the equivalent sections for nodes, labels appear to be successfully extracted from the file, and applied to the node objects.

A work-around is to use the `value` attribute of an edge as a proxy for a label, then use `set_edge_attr_to_display(g, attr = data_value)` to display these as labels on graph visualisations, provided each proxy label matches the value regex `[a-z0-9\\.]*`, as per example.

title: Upcoming changes in igraph lead to revdep issues
description:
Hi,

Just wanted to give a heads up that an upcoming change in `igraph` affects your package. The `neighbors()`function was always intended to only work with one vertex as input and this has now been added as a validation here:
https://github.com/igraph/rigraph/blob/a5c2a3f19900f968b4291c103fdfe1126529476f/R/aaa-auto.R#L193-L198

The `get_leverage_centrality()` function uses the the function with several nodes as input here:
https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/blob/999d742f5eb41d63bf28034d0872591756dd1f89/R/get_leverage_centrality.R#L62-L66

This needs to be replaced with something like
`lapply(seq_along(degree_vals), function(i) neighbors(g, i))`

to work in the future.

Let me know if you need help implementing this change.

                        edges_df = create_edge_df(1, 2, label = "n"))

```

```{r }
library(DiagrammeR)

ndf <-
  create_node_df(
    rankdir = "LR",

title: Test relies on specific output from sample_islands() for given seed

title: rsvg Package should be in Imports, not Suggests
description:
The `export_graph` function calls functions from `rsvg` package, but `rsvg` package is not in Imports, and I didn't have it installed, so the function threw an error.

Also, when I initially used `export_graph` with `filetype = "PNG"`, it threw the following error generated from within your function:

> Error: `export_graph()` REASONS:
> Cannot currently use this function to produce a PNG file
> please install the `DiagrammeRsvg` package and retry

This error was not very helpful, because installing `DiagrammeRsvg` did not fix the problem. Only when I ran `export_graph()` file `filetype = "PDF"` was the following error thrown:

> Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘rsvg’

Only then did I realize that `rsvg` was a dependency, and after installing and loading `rsvg` package, the `export_graph()` function worked, with both file types.

title: Error: "there is no package called 'rsvg'" on Solaris
description:
Today, I received an email from CRAN team about my package [pmap](https://github.com/twang2218/pmap) which depends on `DiagrammeR` package, the mail said:

> See https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_pmap.html (which is still updating).
>
> You are not using the Suggests package rsvg conditionally as required in §1.1.3.1 of the manual.  Please check all other uses of suggested packages, and correct before Mar 22 to safely retain the package on CRAN.

And the logs of the failed part of my package is following:

```R
Version: 0.6.0 
Check: package dependencies 
Result: NOTE 
    Package suggested but not available for checking: ‘rsvg’ 
Flavor: r-patched-solaris-x86

Version: 0.6.0 
Check: tests 
Result: ERROR 
     Running ‘testthat.R’ [28s/30s]
    Running the tests in ‘tests/testthat.R’ failed.
    Complete output:
     > library(testthat)
     > library(pmap)
     > 
     > set.seed(101)
     > 
     > test_check("pmap")
     ── 1. Error: render_pmap_file() should be able to render to a file (@test_render
     there is no package called 'rsvg'
     1: render_pmap_file(p, file_name, format = format) at testthat/test_render_pmap_file.R:15
     2: DiagrammeR::export_graph(p, file_name = file_name, file_type = format, width = width, 
     height = height)
     3: rsvg::rsvg_pdf
     4: getExportedValue(pkg, name)
     5: asNamespace(ns)
     6: getNamespace(ns)
     7: tryCatch(loadNamespace(name), error = function(e) stop(e))
     8: tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
     9: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
     10: value[[3L]](cond)
```

It seems caused by the `DiagrammeR::export_graph()` calling the suggested package `rsvg` without using the conditional pattern recommended at CRAN manual [1.1.3.1](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Suggested-packages).

```R
   if (requireNamespace("rgl", quietly = TRUE)) {
      rgl::plot3d(...)
   } else {
      ## do something else not involving rgl.

title: `generate_dot()` uses single quotes instead of double quotes
description:
Using the `generate_dot()` function, the output uses single quotes around every attribute value, which (as far as I can tell) isn't supported in the `dot` language. Writing the output of `generate_dot()` to a file and subsequently running `dot` from a command line on that file throws a syntax error.

For example:

```r
g <- create_graph() %>%
    add_node() %>%
    add_node() %>%
    add_edge(1,2)

generate_dot(g) %>% writeLines("test.dot")
```

produces
 
```
digraph {

graph [layout = 'neato',
       outputorder = 'edgesfirst',
       bgcolor = 'white']

node [fontname = 'Helvetica',
      fontsize = '10',
      shape = 'circle',
      fixedsize = 'true',
      width = '0.5',
      style = 'filled',
      fillcolor = 'aliceblue',
      color = 'gray70',
      fontcolor = 'gray50']

edge [fontname = 'Helvetica',
     fontsize = '8',
     len = '1.5',
     color = 'gray80',
     arrowsize = '0.5']

  '1'
  '2'
  '1'->'2' 
}
```

and `dot -Tpng test.dot -o test.png` from a command line gives `Error: test.dot: syntax error in line 3 near '''`. However, replacing the single quotes with double quotes (e.g. with `str_replace("'", "\"")`) produces a file that *does* work with command-line `dot`.

It seems to me that `generate_dot()` should use double quotes by default since that's what `dot` expects.

title: Remove required argument ```n``` from create_node_dfs
description:
Both ```create_node_df``` and ```add_node_df``` at the moment offer really little value to the user. Stripped to the core, a node df can be a character vector, with everything else being optional. One could just use a wrapper function to feed a character vector into ```create_node_df``` and if would work 100% of the time. The greatest offender is the required ```n``` argument for ```create_node_df``` which is nothing but an unnecessary math exercise. ```n``` is a function of the ```type``` or ```label``` argument. The way that the arguments are parsed also conceals the fact that the whole thing is nothing but a wrapper around a df with an id, type, and label column.

```add_node_df``` should reflect the reality that users are capable of keeping track of types and labels themselves. Just allow the user to feed in a dataframe and require as a minimum no more than what is absolutely necessary to create a diagram--one column, either ```type``` or ```label``` with ID and everything else being optional. In fact, we don't need to even do any data validation here. As long as a meaningful error message is thrown, the average R user should really be able to figure out what is wrong.

title: `colorize_node_attrs` and `colorize_edge_attrs` do not handle hexadecimal colors not in X11 set
description:
Current implementations of `colorize_node_attrs` and `colorize_edge_attrs` fail when hexadecimal colors are provided that happen not to be in the named `x11_hex()` set. For example, `#64ccc9` is a valid hexadecimal color that is not in `DiagrammeR:::x11_hex()$hex` and therefore the following code will fail:

```
  graph <-
    create_graph() %>%
    add_gnm_graph(
      n = 10,
      m = 22,
      node_data = node_data(
        value = 1:10),
      set_seed = 23) %>%
    colorize_node_attrs(
      node_attr_from = value,
      node_attr_to = fillcolor,
      cut_points = c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9),
      palette = c("#64ccc9", "#8b3e2f", "#00eeee", "#556b2f", "#9932cc",
                  "#698b69", "#cd2626", "#4a4a4a"))
```

I will submit a bugfix with updated tests for this case.

title: Single quotes erroneously replaced with escaped double-quotes
description:
According to the Dot language spec () only the double-quote character should be escaped i.e.  a literal ```"``` should be included in a dot file as ```\"```

In ```grViz()``` however it appears that a single-quote (```'```) is escaped to be ```\"``` :

```diagram <- gsub(x = diagram, "'", "\"")```

This changes any single quotes (for example apostrophes in words) with a double quote character.

E.g. A node label ```they'll``` is erroneously converted into the dot output ```they"ll```

Posslbe fix: Change the ```gsub``` pattern to be ```'"'``` instead of ```"'"```

description:
I am trying to render diagram with icons and I found that the part of code that must render pictures with icons is just not present in **DiagrammeR::render_graph** function that leads to an error.

What I do (in R):

```
SetNodeStyle(
  tree,
  label = function(node) node$FriendlyName,
  shape = "box",
  style = function(node) node$Style,
  imagepath = "C:\\temp",
  image = "icon1.png"
)

plot <- plot(tree)
```

After that I an getting an error:

**Error in DiagrammeR::render_graph(graph, output = output, ...) :

The reason is, plot.node calls DiagrammeR::render_graph:

```
plot.Node <- function(x, ..., direction = c("climb", "descend"), pruneFun = NULL, output = "graph") {
  if(!requireNamespace("DiagrammeR", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop(
      "Package \"DiagrammeR\" is required to plot a `data.tree::Node`",
      "object. Please install it."
    )}
  
  graph <- ToDiagrammeRGraph(x, direction, pruneFun)
  render_graph(graph, output = output, ...)
}

title: Decrease the distance between nodes in the last-to-date DiagrammeR version (1.0.6.1)
description:
I would like to decrease the distance between nodes. I am aware that is a similar question here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38055696/how-to-increase-distance-between-nodes-in-diagrammer-r. However, such a solution is not working in the current DiagrammeR version (1.0.6.1). I have a found in the manual a given solution:

```

library(DiagrammeR)
graph <-
  create_graph() %>%
  add_path(
    n = 3,
    type = "path",
    edge_aes = edge_aes(
      style = "solid",
      color = c("yellow", "blue"),
      len= c(10, 0.2), ## Parameter to change edge distance
    ))

render_graph(graph, layout="tree")
```

As pointed in the code above, the len parameter is supposed to give different distances to the two different edges (i.e. nodes 1-2 to 2-3). However the resulting diagram don´t have different edge distances. I am aware that in the dot language (i.e. Graphviz) the distance between nodes is governed by minlen parameter. However, minlen is not a parameter in the edge_aes(). I even tried to modify the source code of the edge_aes() to include a minlen parameter, but it did not work as well:

```

{

                      fontname = fontname, fontsize = fontsize, fontcolor = fontcolor, 
                      len = len, tooltip = tooltip, URL = URL, label = label, 
                      labelfontname = labelfontname, labelfontsize = labelfontsize, 
                      labelfontcolor = labelfontcolor, labeltooltip = labeltooltip, 
                      labelURL = labelURL, edgetooltip = edgetooltip, edgeURL = edgeURL, 
                      dir = dir, headtooltip = headtooltip, headURL = headURL, 
                      headclip = headclip, headlabel = headlabel, headport = headport, 
                      tailtooltip = tailtooltip, tailURL = tailURL, tailclip = tailclip, 
                      taillabel = taillabel, tailport = tailport, decorate = decorate,
                      minlen=minlen)
  non_null_attrs <- 1:length(attr_values) %>% purrr::map_chr(.f = function(x) {
    if (!is.null(attr_values[[x]])) {

    }

    }

}

title: Vignette for graphviz(/mermaid) appears to miss documentation/tables of valid graphviz node shapes and arrowhead values
description: The vignette for graphviz/mermaid support has a section on graphviz node and arrowhead values here: https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/blob/master/vignettes/graphviz-mermaid.Rmd#L144-L150. It seems to lack a table with the actual valid values for graphviz node shapes and arrowhead values, and corresponding figures. The following R/Rmd snippet would appear to be able to provide the missing information (but has no wrapping so the images become quite wide): ```r library(rvest) library(stringi) library(DiagrammeR) # graphviz node shapes shapes <- # read HTML table from grapviz docs "https://www.graphviz.org/doc/info/shapes.html" %>% read_html() %>% html_table(fill = TRUE) %>% # subset/index to get the shapes `[[`(1) %>% with(., c(X1, X2, X3, X4)) %>% stri_remove_empty_na() shapes_gallery <- sprintf("a%s[shape = @@1-%s, label = @@1-%s];", 1:length(shapes), 1:length(shapes), 1:length(shapes)) %>% paste0(collapse = "\n") shapes_gv <- sprintf("digraph shapes {%s}\n[1]: shapes", shapes_gallery) # available shapes message("valid gv node shape values are:") shapes %>% paste0(collapse = ", ") %>% cat # figure with all the available shapes grViz(shapes_gv, width = 2048 * 2) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(grViz(shapes_gv, width = 2048), file = "~/shapes.html") # graphviz arrowheads arrowheads <- "https://www.graphviz.org/doc/info/arrows.html" %>% read_html() %>% html_table(fill = TRUE) %>% `[[`(4) %>% with(., c(X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6)) %>% stringi::stri_remove_empty_na() n <- length(arrowheads) arrowheads_gallery <- sprintf("a%s -> b%s [arrowhead = @@1-%s, label = @@1-%s];", 1:n, 1:n, 1:n, 1:n) %>% paste0(collapse = "\n") arrowheads_gv <- sprintf("digraph arrowheads {%s}\n[1]: arrowheads", arrowheads_gallery) # available arrowheads message("valid gv arrowhead values are:") arrowheads %>% paste0(collapse = ", ") %>% cat # figure with all the arrowheads grViz(arrowheads_gv, width = 2048) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(grViz(arrowheads_gv, width = 2048), file = "~/arrowheads.html") ``` Valid shape node values seem to be: box, circle, plaintext, parallelogram, septagon, tripleoctagon, Mdiamond, rectangle, underline, folder, cds, restrictionsite, assembly, rnastab, rarrow, polygon, point, plain, house, octagon, invtriangle, Msquare, square, cylinder, box3d, terminator, fivepoverhang, signature, proteasesite, larrow, ellipse, egg, diamond, pentagon, doublecircle, invtrapezium, Mcircle, star, note, component, utr, threepoverhang, insulator, proteinstab, lpromoter, oval, triangle, trapezium, hexagon, doubleoctagon, invhouse, rect, none, tab, promoter, primersite, noverhang, ribosite, rpromoter Valid arrowhead values seem to be: box, crow, diamond, dot, inv, none, normal, tee, vee, curve, lbox, lcrow, ldiamond, odot, linv, lnormal, ltee, lvee, lcurve, rbox, rcrow, rdiamond, rinv, rnormal, rtee, rvee, rcurve, obox, odiamond, oinv, onormal, icurve, olbox, oldiamond, olinv, olnormal, licurve, orbox, ordiamond, orinv, ornormal, ricurve>

title: Add arrow shapes that support crow's foot notation (more options for arrowhead and arrowtail)
description:
Thanks for creating this package! I think that `DiagrammeR` is a great way to visualise data warehouse table entity relationship diagrams. A common way to draw these diagrams is via crow's foot notation, as depicted below. Whilst `crow` and `tee` arrow shapes can be used to mimic the concept of many and one, extra arrow types might be useful to denote:  

+ zero or one (combination of a `dot` and `tee` ?)
+ zero or many (combination of a `dot` and `crow`?)
+ one or many (combination of a `tee` and `crow`?) 

![](https://res.cloudinary.com/practicaldev/image/fetch/s--aMHSzLpu--/c_limit%2Cf_auto%2Cfl_progressive%2Cq_auto%2Cw_880/https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/gjzq00ltrbmxqjx7i1wp.PNG)  

Otherwise, this is my current closest approximation to visualising a data warehouse ERD with a combination of a crow's nest like and Chen's notation. 

```
my_ERD <- grViz("digraph {

          graph[layout = dot, rankdir = 'LR'] 
          
          node[shape = rectangle, style = filled, fillcolor = 'linen', fontsize = 12]
          
          subgraph cluster_patient { 
             graph[rankdir = TB, label = 'Patient Table', fontsize = 18, 
                   shape = rectangle, color = 'sandybrown', style = dashed]

             a[label = 'PatientID']
             b[label = 'CreatedDate']
             c[label = 'HospitalSite']
             
          }
             
          subgraph cluster_procedure { 
             graph[rankdir = TB, label = 'Procedure Table', fontsize = 18, 
                   shape = rectangle, color = 'lightsalmon', style = dashed]

             d[label = 'ProcedureID']
             e[label = 'ProcedureStartDate']
             f[label = 'ProcedureFinishDate'] 
             
          }
          
          subgraph cluster_invoice { 
             graph[rankdir = TB, label = 'Invoice Table', fontsize = 18, 
                   shape = rectangle, color = 'lightsalmon', style = dashed]

             g[label = 'InvoiceID']
             h[label = 'InvoiceCost']
             i[label = 'CreatedDate']
             j[label = 'PaidDate']
             
          } 
          
          edge[color = black, dir = 'both', style = 'dashed']
               
              a -> d[arrowhead = 'crow', arrowtail = 'tee', label = '1 : N'] # use Chen's notation to label edges for clarity 
              d -> g[arrowhead = 'tee', arrowtail = 'tee', label = '1 : 1'] 
          
          }")

my_ERD
```   
![2020-06-06_flowchart-ERD](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34994264/85921533-44756f80-b8c0-11ea-8e63-297b5690f165.png)

title: DiagrammeR setting opacity to low
description:
I've been trying to use DiagrammeR::mermaid to render a flowchart in my RMarkdown document. However, when I knit the .Rmd, most of the rendered document is faded out.

MWE:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48382869/75390276-e91a7d00-58df-11ea-99fb-644412704f17.png)

Output:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48382869/75390379-1535fe00-58e0-11ea-9b42-b8c27f0a77c2.png)

If I get rid of the header (i.e. drop the # in the This is a Test line), then it renders fine.

After investigating, I found that the header of the rendered HTML file contains the following lines (between a `<style>` and `</style>` command):

`.mermaid-main-font {`
`font-family: "trebuchet ms", verdana, arial;`
`font-family: var(--mermaid-font-family);`
`}`
`.section {`
`stroke: none;`
`opacity: 0.2;`
`}`

This is setting the class "section" to have opacity 0.2, and unfortunately the entire document that gets rendered inherits this. I'm not sure where or why this piece of CSS gets inserted.

A workaround for this is to insert the code
`<style>`
`.section{`
`opacity:1;`
`}`
`</style>`
somewhere in the .Rmd (or in a separate linked css sheet). This overrides the styling placed in the header by mermaid.

I post this here as an Issue hoping that there might be a possible bug fix added to DiagrammeR in future, or at the very least to provide the workaround as a solution for others who may have this problem.

title: endless loop in replace_in_spec
description:
First, thank you for this awesome package and documentation piece!

I experienced an endless loop, which I traced down to `replace_in_spec`, precisely [here](https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/blob/4bf69537405d49e5cb24f05dc3cbf4cf8c9b5db2/R/spectools.R#L107).
I can see that the code attempts to replace `'@@<number>'` (mind the surrounding single quotes). If no replacement occurs, the while loop continues infinitely.

When I noticed the endless loop my graph definition was

```graphviz
digraph syntax {
...
node [ fontcolor = @@1 ]
...
[1]: global_fontcolor
}
```
I tried changing `@@1` to `"@@1"` but no joy, then I looked at the source code and discovered that the only valid syntax to affect the replacement is `'@@1'` (tested, works).  This [document](https://rich-iannone.github.io/DiagrammeR/graphviz_and_mermaid.html#substitution) - section _Graphviz Substitution_ / _How It Works_ - makes no mention of the single quote requirement.

While this is an issue, users can easily work around it by ensuring surrounding single quotes for all `@@<number>` references.

Note: I didn't test `@@<number>-<index>` references.

title: Implementation of rank when using functions?
Update to D3 v4 to combine netword3D and mermaid in Rmarkdown
description:
This is essentially a repost of [this question on Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44981095/combining-netword3d-and-mermaid-in-rmarkdown-messes-up-rendering) which I also raised as an issue with the `htmlwidgets` package. 

I would like to include two `htmlwidgets` in the same Rmarkdown document - a `mermaid` flowchart from the `DiagrammeR` package and a `network3D` graph. If I include both in my document then none of them renders but if I only include one of them then it will be rendered. 

Here's a minimal example in Rmarkdown that shows the problem

    ---
    title: "Untitled"
    author: "Me"
    output: html_document
    ---
    
    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
    ```
    
    ## The grViz always works

    ```{r dia1, echo=FALSE}
    library(DiagrammeR)
    grViz("
      digraph {
        layout = twopi
        A -> {B C D}
      }")
    ```
    
    # From here onwards I can only include one of the two graphs 
    
    ```{r}
    mermaid("
    graph LR
        A-->B
    ")
    ```
    
    # Plot
    
    ```{r}
    library(networkD3)
    Source <- c("A", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C", "D")
    Target <- c("B", "C", "D", "J", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I")
    NetworkData <- data.frame(Source, Target)
    
    # Create graph
    simpleNetwork(NetworkData)
    ```
    

If I add multiple `DiagrammeR` graphs based on `grViz` then all is fine and dandy. Also if I leave out the `mermaid` plot then I'll see the remaining two. Are they not supposed to play together nicely? I've tried to swap the ordering of the `library` calls to no avail.

ramnath told me that
>  `networkD3` uses D3 v 4, while `diagrammeR` uses D3 v 3. D3 v 4 introduced a lot of breaking 
> changes in the API. This is the reason these two widgets are not playing nicely. You can ping the author of diagrammeR to see if he can update it to using D3 v 4.

so ... any plans for upgrading to D3 v4?

title: Non-random graphs shouldn't change the RNG state
description:
Minimal example:

```r
set.seed(123)
head(.Random.seed)
#> [1]      10403        624 -983674937  643431772 1162448557 -959247990
DiagrammeR::create_graph()
#> DiagrammeR Graph // no nodes
#>  ...
head(.Random.seed) # changed!
#> [1]      10403         16  515190382 2133433928  917665867 1283494313
```

This is because `create_graph()` calls `sample` to create a unique ID. This is unexpected from the user's perspective, and I don't think it's reasonable to change the RNG state for this. It *is* expected if we are creating a random graph (and still, it should be documented), but not in any other case. (This may happen in other places too, but I didn't check thoroughly).

title: Integrate grViz figures into bookdown
description:
I reviewed #256, #70, #207, #133 but couldn't quite find a solution.

A plot generated in a `knitr` chunk (e.g. by ggplot) gets saved as a figure with a filename that is passed from the chunk label, in `_bookdown_files` directory. The same is not done with `grViz` figures. To emulate this behaviour, one can do the following to both print and save a `grViz` figure
``` r
library(magrittr)
g <- DiagrammeR::grViz('digraph{a->b; c->a; c->b; c->d;}')
g
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/o3LrnUR.png)

``` r
g %>%
  DiagrammeRsvg::export_svg() %>%
  charToRaw() %>%
  rsvg::rsvg_png("g.png")
```

<sup>Created on 2019-04-25 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

But this does not programatically pass the chunk label to the `png` file name and put it in the same directory as the other saved figures.

title: interactivity and other features
description:
@pommedeterresautee Since Issue #7 began as a discussion about _CRAN integration_, I thought it would be good to start this new thread that isolates and tracks the discussion about additional features, primarily interactivity.  I hope this is ok.

> Does anyone know if in Shiny it's possible to collapse a branch of a generated tree? (like you click on a node and the branch after the node are collapsed)

Very little of the first round of `mermaid.js` development (parsing and rendering) has focused on interactivity, but there is [support for callbacks](http://knsv.github.io/mermaid/flowchart.html#interaction) within its markdown-like spec that we could use.

title: `image` attribute of `dot` does not work
description:
I learned it is possible to add an image to a node from [the documentation](https://graphviz.gitlab.io/_pages/doc/info/attrs.html#d:image) of `dot` languge.

>image 
>
>Gives the name of a file containing an image to be displayed inside a node. The image file must be in one of the recognized formats, typically JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, SVG or Postscript, and be able to be converted into the desired output format. 
>
> The file must contain the image size information. This is usually trivially true for the bitmap formats. For PostScript, the file must contain a line starting with %%BoundingBox: followed by four integers specifying the lower left x and y coordinates and the upper right x and y coordinates of the bounding box for the image, the coordinates being in points. An SVG image file must contain width and height attributes, typically as part of the svg element. The values for these should have the form of a floating point number, followed by optional units, e.g., width="76pt". Recognized units are in, px, pc, pt, cm and mm for inches, pixels, picas, points, centimeters and millimeters, respectively. The default unit is points. 
Unlike with the shapefile attribute, the image is treated as node content rather than the entire node. In particular, an image can be contained in a node of any shape, not just a rectangle. 

[Here](https://graphviz.gitlab.io/_pages/Gallery/directed/kennedyanc.html) is an example. But it does not work in `grViz`.

Thanks for making DiagrammeR! ## Mermaid Using `DiagrammeR(diagram = "", type = "mermaid")` it's possible to use HTML tags in the node labels: library("DiagrammeR") DiagrammeR("graph TB; A{Is your data public?} -- yes -->C; A -- no -->B[

B [label = 'Please make it public']; C [label = 'Tech Question']; D [label = 'Supported' ]; E [label = 'Unsupported!']; F [label = 'Refer to our tutorial'] # several 'edge' statements A->B A->C C->D [label = 'yes'] C->E [label = 'no'] C->F [label = 'Unknown'] } ") This doesn't support HTML tags: grViz(" digraph boxes_and_circles { # a 'graph' statement graph [overlap = true, fontsize = 10] # several 'node' statements node [shape = box, fontname = Helvetica] A [label = 'Is your data public?']; title: exporting mermaid chart directly to png
description:
I would like to export a chart created with `mermaid()` directly to a simple image file (ex: .png) from within an executed .R script without going through the graphical export menus of RStudio.

This has previously come up in the closed issue:  
https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/issues/174 'export_graph does not work with mermaid'


In that issue, an error was produced while trying to use the `export_graph()` function to create .png output from charts generated by the `mermaid()` and `DiagrammeR()` functions.

Issue https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/issues/174 was closed, but I'm still having problems when I try:  

    library("DiagrammeR")
    mg <- mermaid("graph TB
      A-->B")
    export_graph(mg,'mg.png')
Which results in:  
`Error in export_graph(mg, "mg.png") : The graph object is not valid.`

I've tried this with the CRAN-available version of DiagrammeR in both Windows and Linux (debian/kubuntu) environments, inside and outside RStudio, with `DiagrammeRsvg` and `rsvg` packages installed as recommended by error messages.

The chart (in this case, the htmlwidget object `mg`) renders successfully to the RStudio plot window.  From a console session outside RStudio it opens the system's default internet browser window to display the image.  

Despite the htmlwidget object working correctly in those contexts, attempting to use `export_graph()` on it to directly create an image file results in the error described above.

In the `export_graph()` documentation, there is the following line:  
`graph: a graph object of class ‘dgr_graph’.`

Which explains the error message if htmlwidget objects are not supported by this function.

However, back in the closed issue [#174](https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/issues/174) in the comments, it was stated:
>This is currently a limitation but I will work on making 'export_graph()' produce graphical output files with mermaid and Graphviz graph definitions.

And on the [I/O page](http://rich-iannone.github.io/DiagrammeR/io.html) of the DiagrammeR docs:
> Aside from viewing/exporting, there are several workflows for creating DiagrammeR output such as **through R scripts**, R Markdown, and with Shiny apps.  

So it looks like direct from code export (possibly with the `export_graph()` function) is intended to be supported for `mermaid()` charts, but I can't find a description on that page of how to implement any R script workflows, and the `export_graph()` function still seems incompatible with `mermaid()` charts.

Is there something I am missing, that enables a direct export of `mermaid()` charts to simple image file formats like .png?

Is this something that is still under development?

Thanks!

title: from_igraph() drops vertex character names
description:
See [this StackOverflow post](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/42985152/problems-converting-igraph-to-diagrammer-graph). I reproduced the issue for the current CRAN version (0.9.0) and commit a77fc20d13a3ad654148fe37a7ac3e5ae16bb5a1.

```r
library(igraph)
library(DiagrammeR)
g = make_empty_graph() + vertices(c("a", "b")) + edge("a", "b")
x = from_igraph(g)
```

The [drake package](https://github.com/wlandau-lilly/drake) internally relies on `igraph` objects with meaningful vertex names, and `DiagrammeR` has such powerful visuals.

`%not_in%` <- Negate(`%in%`)

loadings

I tried to manually add the missing edges by `add_edge()`, there is no problem. But whenever I use `add_edges_from_table()` there always many edges are missing.

After many try and fail, I decided to read the source code of `add_edges_from_table()` function, and then I found following undocumented behavior at <https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/blob/0.9.2/R/add_edges_from_table.R#L195-L203>:

```R
  # Expand the df to capture several space-delimited
  # values in the `to` column; drop NA values in the
  # `to_col` and the `from_col` columns
  csv <-
    csv %>%
    dplyr::mutate_(.dots = setNames(paste0("strsplit(", to_col, ", \" \")"), to_col)) %>%
    tidyr::unnest_(to_col) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na_(to_col) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na_(from_col)
```

Which basically says, if the content of `to` column contains `<SPACE>`, it will be treated as **space-delimited values** and be splitted and unnested. This behavior caused me the trouble, my node names contains space, which is valid for GraphViz.

Here is the demo code to show the problem:

```R
library(DiagrammeR)

cites <- data.frame(
  name = c("Sydney", "Los Angeles", "New York", "Beijing"),
  stringsAsFactors = F
)

paths <- data.frame(
  from  = c("Sydney", "Sydney", "Los Angeles", "Beijing"),
  to    = c("Beijing", "New York", "New York", "Los Angeles"),
  stringsAsFactors = F
)

p <- create_graph()
p <- add_nodes_from_table(p, cites, label_col = "name")
p <- add_edges_from_table(p, paths, from_col = "from", to_col = "to", ndf_mapping = "name")

print("str(paths):")
print(str(paths))
#  Output:
# [1] "str(paths):"
# 'data.frame':	4 obs. of  2 variables:
#  $ from: chr  "Sydney" "Sydney" "Los Angeles" "Beijing"
#  $ to  : chr  "Beijing" "New York" "New York" "Los Angeles"
# NULL

edge_df <- get_edge_df(p)
print("str(edge_df):")
print(str(edge_df))
# Output:
# [1] "str(edge_df):"
# 'data.frame':	1 obs. of  4 variables:
#  $ id  : int 1
#  $ from: int 1
#  $ to  : int 4
#  $ rel : chr NA
# NULL
```

As you can see, only `"Sydney" -> "Beijing"` remain, all other edges are missing.

title: Can't get graphviz script to run in DiagrammeR
Setting of graph layout is ambiguous
description:
`render_graph()` has an argument `layout` that is only used for `vivagraph`. The layout for graphviz needs to be set with something like 
```r
 g <-
   g %>%DiagrammeR::set_global_graph_attrs("layout","dot",attr_type = "graph")
```
Yet, the value of `layout` is available when `render_graph` calls `generate_dot()` (https://github.com/rich-iannone/DiagrammeR/blob/master/R/render_graph.R#L120). The layout should be passed and override any layout set in the graph object. 

Furthermore `create_graph()` should set a default layout of `dot` instead of `neato` for directed graphs. This is what a user expects when no layout is given and corresponds to behaviour pre-DiagrammeR-0.9
As http://graphviz.org/ says:
> ***dot*** - "hierarchical" or layered drawings of directed graphs. This is the default tool to use if edges have directionality.

title: Poor performance in get_eccentricity
v0.9.1 no longer compatible with R-oldrel (3.3.3)
description:
The latest `DiagrammeR` version depends on `grDevices >= 3.4.0`. Since this is a base package, you really should be defining the dependency against the R version instead (R >= 3.4.0) to prevent errors on earlier R versions.

For example, `DiagrammeR` fails to install on R-oldrel (3.3.3):

```r

** package ‘DiagrammeR’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** R
** inst
** tests
** preparing package for lazy loading
Error in loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]) : 
  namespace ‘grDevices’ 3.3.3 is already loaded, but >= 3.4.0 is required
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘DiagrammeR’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/DiagrammeR’
```

See also a recent [r-pkg-devel thread](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2017q3/001753.html).

title: Keep character nodes after combine_nodes()
description:
The last bit of the `combine_nodes()` function

``` R
df_new[, 1] <-
  as.integer(df_new[, 1])
```

if the _nodes_ are characters (e.g. "z", "a", "b") they become integers (e.g. "3", "1", "2"). 

As a consequence the following `add_edge_df()` after `add_node_df()` example fails:

``` R
library(DiagrammeR)
library(magrittr)

create_nodes(
  nodes = c(
    "a", "b"
  ),
  label = c(
    "A", "B"
  )
) -> nodes

create_graph(
  nodes_df = nodes
) -> g0

# check the nodes
g0$nodes_df

g0 %>%
  add_node_df(
    node_df = create_nodes(
      nodes = "c",
      label = "C"
    )
  ) -> g1

# check the nodes
g1$nodes_df  # the nodes identifiers have changed to integers

# then it fails
g1 %>%
  add_edge_df(
    edge_df = create_edges(
      from = "a",
      to = "b"
    )
  ) ->  g2
```

Would you want to:
- add a condition for the `as.integer(df_new[, 1])` so in case one of the dataframes nodes are character then do `as.character(df_new[, 1])`
- or you think that nodes should only be integers?
- or something else?

Happy to make the change and send you a pull request if that'd be helpful.

Thanks

title: Incorrect international symbols: parameter `encoding = "UTF-8"` in `grViz` is needed
description:
I use international symbols in my DiagrammeR plots. Function `grViz` internally uses `readLines`. Unfortunately, there is no possibility to pass parameter `encoding`  to `readLines` via `grViz`. This leads to incorrect international symbols in my diagrams. I'd like to ask to **add parameter `encoding`** (or equivalent) **with default value set to `"UTF-8"`** to function `grViz`.

_The illustration of my problem._

Contents of file "analysis_main.gv":

```
digraph International_symbols {
      A  [label = "Ąą Čč Ęę Ėė Įį"]
      C  [label = "Šš Ųų Ūū Žž"]
     A -> C;
 }
```

When I press _"Preview"_ button in RStudio, the international symbols are displayed incorrectly:  
![rplot01](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/12725868/17703928/fbf0599c-63db-11e6-86bb-8a061fa1fcbc.jpeg)

When I use following code, the result is also incorrect:

```
library(magrittr)

#  >>> INCORRECT RESULT <<< :(
"analysis_main.gv"     %>% 
DiagrammeR::grViz()

#  >>> INCORRECT RESULT <<< :(
"analysis_main.gv"     %>%
    readLines()                   %>%
    paste0(collapse = "\n")       %>% 
    DiagrammeR::grViz()
```

But when I add `encoding = "UTF-8"` the problem is **solved**:

```
#  >>> CORRECT RESULT <<< :)
"analysis_main.gv"     %>%
    readLines(encoding = "UTF-8") %>%
    paste0(collapse = "\n")       %>% 
    DiagrammeR::grViz()

```

title: DOT code is constant, but the generated graph flips between 2 very different-looking graphs
description:
This is very strange.  This problem occurs in a Shiny app.  I noticed that the graphs being rendered were sometimes correct and sometimes incorrect.  So, to remove all the possible sources of error in my code, I even changed the renderGrViz code to use _constant_ DOT code for the graph.  Even then, it _still_ flips (primarily) between two different outputs.

One clue is that (even in the minimal Shiny app at the bottom of this comment), the first graph generated is always correct.  So there must be some internal state information that is causing the mis-renderings.  This suggests that, in lieu of a bug fix, there might be a workaround that involves re-initializing the internal state of a library (?).

This is the code:

```
output$diagram <- renderGrViz({
    # This code is here just to have a reactive dependency that triggers re-running this renderGrViz
    if (isTRUE(input$flag)) {

That slight variation, which occurs about 1% to 2% of the time, looks like this:

title: edge_info.R error
description:
If you load both `ggplot2` and `diagrammeR`, and create a graph _without_ a column named `rel` in your edge data frame, then you'd see an error message when you do `edge_info(graph)` telling you that you are trying to subset a function. As it turns out, `ggplot2` defines a function `rel`. So the following check in `edge_info.R`, line 82, will return True, and you end up subsetting the ggplot2 function `rel()`.

```
      edge_properties[i, 3] <-
        ifelse(exists("rel"),
               rel[which((edge_from %in% edge_from[i]) &
                           (edge_to %in% edge_to[i]))],
               rep(NA, length(edge_from)))
```

This can be fixed with

```
ifelse("rel" %in% colnames(graph$edges_df),
```

which was the test to create 'rel'.

title: delete_node fix
description:
I came across an issue with the current delete_node function. When a node in the graph has no edges, it gives the following error:

```
Error in if (all(!(colnames(edges_df)[j] %in% c("edgetooltip", "headtooltip",  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

It seems the problem is that edges_df is actually empty because the lines

``` r
 # Create a revised edge data frame
 revised_edges_df <- graph$edges_df[-which((graph$edges_df$from == node) |
                                                (graph$edges_df$to == node)),]
```

produce an empty dataframe instead of keeping the original one.

I've written a quick fix, that works for me.

``` r
    # Create a revised edge data frame
    if (nrow(graph$edges_df[-which((graph$edges_df$from == node) |
                                    (graph$edges_df$to == node)),]) == 0) {
      revised_edges_df <- graph$edges_df
    } else {
      revised_edges_df <- graph$edges_df[-which((graph$edges_df$from == node) |
                                                  (graph$edges_df$to == node)),]
    }
```

What do yo think?

Thanks,

title: Shiny apps that use DiagrammeR don't work when deployed on shinyapps.io or Shiny Server Pro
description:
This happens because Shiny Server inserts a `<base>` tag in the HTML body, which causes problems with some SVG elements, like arrowheads and gradients.

Fortunately, the latest version of mermaid.js has a fix for this (thanks to yours truly), so simply including the latest version should fix it for DiagrammeR. See knsv/mermaid#209 for more information about this problem.

title: Error in example
description:
I used the sample code from the main page:

``` r
library("DiagrammeR") 
library("nycflights13")
library("lubridate")
library("magrittr")

# Choose a day from 2013 for NYC flight data
# (You can choose any Julian day, it's interesting to see results for different days)
day_of_year <- 10 

# Get a data frame of complete cases (e.g., flights have departure and arrival times)
nycflights13 <-
  nycflights13::flights[which(complete.cases(nycflights13::flights) == TRUE), ]

# Generate a POSIXct vector of dates using the 'ISOdatetime' function
# Columns 1, 2, and 3 are year, month, and day columns
# Column 4 is a 4-digit combination of hours (00-23) and minutes (00-59)
date_time <-
  data.frame("date_time" =
               ISOdatetime(year = nycflights13[,1],
                           month = nycflights13[,2],
                           day = nycflights13[,3],
                           hour = gsub("[0-9][0-9]$", "", nycflights13[,4]),
                           min = gsub(".*([0-9][0-9])$", "\\1", nycflights13[,4]),
                           sec = 0, tz = "GMT"))

# Add the POSIXct vector 'date_time' to the 'nycflights13' data frame
nycflights13 <- cbind(date_time, nycflights13)

# Select flights only from the specified day of the year 2013
nycflights13_day <-
  subset(nycflights13,
         date_time >= ymd('2013-01-01', tz = "GMT") + days(day_of_year - 1) &
           date_time < ymd('2013-01-01', tz = "GMT") + days(day_of_year))

# Create the node data frame
# Column 12 is the 3-letter code for the airport departing from
# Column 13 is for the airport arriving to
# (Option: change df to 'nycflights13_day' and only airports used for the day will be included)
nodes_df <- create_nodes(nodes = unique(c(nycflights13[,12],
                                    nycflights13[,13])),
                         label = FALSE)

# The edge data frame must have columns named 'from' and 'to'
# The color attribute is determined with an 'ifelse' statement, where
# column 8 is the minutes early (negative values) or minutes late (positive values)
# for the flight arrival
edges_df <- create_edges(from = nycflights13_day[,12],
                         to = nycflights13_day[,13],
                         color = ifelse(nycflights13_day[,8] < 0,
                                    "green", "red"))

# Set the graph diagram's default attributes for...

# ...nodes
node_attrs <- c("style = filled", "fillcolor = lightblue",
                "color = gray", "shape = circle", "fontname = Helvetica",
                "width = 1")

# ...edges

# ...and the graph itself

                 "fixedsize = true",
                 "ranksep = 3",
                 "outputorder = edgesfirst")

# Generate the graph diagram in the RStudio Viewer.
create_graph(nodes_df = nodes_df, edges_df = edges_df,
               graph_attrs = graph_attrs, node_attrs = node_attrs,
               edge_attrs = edge_attrs, directed = TRUE) %>%
  render_graph(width = 1200, height = 800)
```

When I try to execute the code, there is an error

```

docs for rstudio previewing / graphviz engine specification
description:
We are planning on releasing a new RStudio Preview on Tuesday that will have the new mermaid.js and graphviz authoring features in it. Once we have this I think it would be good to provide:

(a) A link to the preview release page so that users get the right version

(b) An example (perhaps a screenshot)

(c) Perhaps update the graphviz docs on engines to show how to specify the engine directly as a graph attribute (e.g. `layout = neato`). This is because RStudio calls DiagrammeR with the default arguments so there's no way to preview a non-default engine unless it's specified as part of the graphviz definition. 

If this is viewed as problematic we could do one other thing: allow the user to include a comment that notifies any previewer of the preferred engine. We do something similar to this for Sweave engines (this in turn was adapted from the behavior of popular LaTeX editors). e.g. you can add `% !Rnw weave = knitr` at the top of a Sweave document to tell us to preview it with knitr rather than Sweave. So we could do something like this:

``` cpp
// !Graphviz engine = neato
```

This is obviously one more thing to implement and learn so if it's considered generally okay to put the engine in the graphviz definition that's simpler and thus preferred. Let me know what you think either way so I can get this into the preview for Tuesday.

title: Add razor-like syntax for substituting results of evaluated R expressions (provided in a Markdown-like style as footnotes)
description:
Begun some preliminary work on this. The idea is to allow a marker (I've chosen the double ampersand, followed by a number) to be placed in the graph spec. As numbered footnotes, R expressions are to be provided. After some basic checking, the expressions would be evaluated and the results substituted in the proper locations in the graph spec. As this evolves a bit, I'll provide a workable example. I'd like to support expressions that produce vectors, as well. 

Why do this at all? Hoping that this separation of (very useful) calculation and graph specs will result in better readability and more simplicity for the user. Again, more details to come...

title: fix duplicate svg ids assigned by mermaid
description:
`mermaid.js` must have an internal counter on `mermaid.init()` to assign the `id` to the `SVG` container for the diagram.  In `DiagrammeR`, we set `startOnLoad = F` to suspend the auto-render behavior of `mermaid.js` and then run `mermaid.init()` each time we process a widget.  If only one widget then fine, but if we have >1 widget, then the `mermaidChart0` gets assigned to each `SVG` and everything breaks.  I'll probably file an issue with `mermaid.js` but for now, change the render behavior in `DiagrammeR` to suspend `mermaid.init()` until the last widget.  However, we will likely run into trouble even with this method in a `Shiny` context.

reproducible example of problem:

```
library(DiagrammeR)
library(htmltools)

dg = DiagrammeR("graph LR; A;")

html_print(tagList(dg,dg))
```
